item.title: Surface Nitrogen enrichment from the LMC to the Early Universe: the roles of rotation, overshooting and mass loss
item.description: arXiv:2611.03798v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The strong nitrogen (N) features observed in high-redshift galaxies, such as GN-z11, with JWST point to an efficient source of N production in the early Universe. Very massive stars (VMSs) are promising candidates owing to their strong winds and large convective cores of CNO-processed material. Whether massive-star surfaces in general become N-enriched depends on the interplay of convective-boundary mixing (overshooting), rotation, and mass loss, which remains poorly constrained. Using a grid of MESA evolutionary models, we isolate the overshooting and rotation channels at $40$, $100$, and $200\,M_\odot$ and investigate how these channels bring N-rich material to the surface of massive and very massive stars as a function of initial mass and metallicity. We also construct a synthetic Large Magellanic Cloud (LMC) population based on a larger initial mass grid ranging from $20-300\,M_\odot$ for comparison with the observed N-enriched fraction. VMS surface enrichment is remarkably robust across cosmic metallicity. At lower metallicities, wind stripping is weaker and the overshooting channel shuts off entirely, yet a modest amount of rotation of $\sim90\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$ alone still enriches the surface. At higher metallicity, stronger winds dominate and uncover the core almost independently of the adopted mixing. The two channels operate through physically distinct mechanisms: overshooting enriches the surface only once winds strip the envelope down into the N-rich layers left by the receding core, giving an abrupt jump. Rotation, by contrast, mixes N outward continuously through the layers above the core, producing a gradual rise. Applied to the LMC, a population with modest rotation drawn from the observed velocity distribution and modest overshooting reproduces the observed N-enriched fraction without large core boundary mixing efficiencies otherwise required by non-rotating models.
item.dc:creator: Gautham N. Sabhahit, Jorick. S Vink

item.title: Towards Self-consistent Modeling of Quasi-Stars and their NLTE Spectra: Implications for Little Red Dots
item.description: arXiv:2611.03819v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quasi-stars, massive envelopes surrounding rapidly accreting black hole (BH) seeds, are promising candidates for explaining the rapid formation of supermassive black holes in the early Universe and may account for some of the JWST-discovered Little Red Dots (LRDs). We present a self-consistent framework combining stellar evolution calculations with non-local thermodynamic equilibrium (NLTE) spectral synthesis to test this connection. Our models drop the polytropic assumptions of previous work: the envelope is described entirely by mixing-length theory, with saturated convection and radiative energy setting the luminosity at an inner boundary a few hundred Schwarzschild radii from the BH. This removes the BH-mass limits of earlier models, and we follow the evolution up to BH-to-total mass ratios approaching unity. We then use TLUSTY to compute the first converged NLTE atmospheric models for the surface conditions and primordial hydrogen-helium composition expected in quasi-stars. Our models produce cool photospheres, prominent Balmer breaks, and Balmer and Paschen absorption features. NLTE effects substantially modify line strengths, increasing Balmer absorption depths by $\sim 35-55\%$ relative to LTE models, while having a minor effect on the continuum. Comparison with observed LRD spectral energy distributions shows broad agreement in continuum shape, although our models do not reproduce their commonly observed strong emission lines. Under the quasi-star interpretation, comparisons with individual LRDs suggest characteristic quasi-star masses of approximately $10^5-10^7 M_\odot$. These results establish a physically motivated connection between quasi-star evolution and observable spectra, providing a framework for testing quasi-stars as progenitors of LRDs while identifying limitations of current atmospheric models.
item.dc:creator: Jake B. Hassan, Rosalba Perna, Mitchell C. Begelman, Yan-Fei Jiang, Matteo Cantiello, Philip J. Armitage, Taeho Ryu

item.title: Shadowing the Sun I: Testing Synthetic Granulation Spectra with NEID Solar Eclipse Observations
item.description: arXiv:2611.03898v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The subtle Doppler radial velocity (RV) signature of an Earth-mass exoplanet in the Habitable Zone around a nearby Sun-like star is difficult to detect due to stellar variability. While multiple techniques aim to mitigate rotationally-modulated stellar activity, granulation, introducing 0.1-1 m s$^{-1}$ RV shifts, currently sets the floor for detecting Earth-mass RV signals for low-activity stars. Observations of the Rossiter-McLaughlin (RM) effect during a solar eclipse, with a peak-to-trough amplitude of $\sim$1.4 km s$^{-1}$, are a rigorous test of granulation and convective blueshift in the solar spectrum. Using NEID solar feed data of the October 2023 solar eclipse and GRASS-E (a geometry-modified version of GRASS), we compare the observed RVs for 22 lines with the simulated RVs from the synthetic granulation-driven spectra. Residuals of the GRASS-E Fe I 5434 angstrom model show an RMS of 13.47 m s$^{-1}$ over the RM signal. We find that a model with an optimized convective blueshift polynomial for Fe I 5434 significantly outperforms GRASS-E with an RMS of only 2.90 m s$^{-1}$, suggesting that GRASS-E is currently limited by sparse center-to-limb observations. By combining a set of spectral lines, we achieve a weighted RMS of 5.2 m s$^{-1}$ over the RM signal ($\sim$0.37\%), a level of accuracy well beyond the reach of current exoplanet transit observations. In all, we demonstrate that solar eclipse observations allow us to recover the center-to-limb variation of the convective blueshift for individual spectral lines.

item.title: Protostellar evolution of intermediate-mass stars: implications for the survival of fossil magnetic fields
item.description: arXiv:2611.03919v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The detection of strong magnetic fields in radiative stars, particularly chemically peculiar Ap/Bp stars, has motivated various scenarios regarding their origin, including the fossil field hypothesis. Because field survival depends strongly on stellar internal structure, determining when protostars transition from convective to radiative states is essential to assess whether fossil fields persist. We determine the characteristic mass at which intermediate-mass protostars transition from convective to radiative interiors, exploring how this transition favors magnetic field survival. Using the 1D stellar evolution code MESA, we model the pre-main-sequence evolution of intermediate-mass protostars from convective initial seeds across different metallicities, average accretion rates, and accretion histories. The transition mass from predominantly convective to radiative states depends on both accretion rate and metallicity, occurring between $\sim 1.3\,M_\odot$ and $2.8\,M_\odot$ for $1\,M_\odot$ reference models (and up to $\sim 4\,M_\odot$ for other initial masses at high accretion rates). Accretion history details play a secondary role compared to the average rate and metallicity. Lower metallicities shift the transition to lower masses. For $Z \ge 0.01$ and accretion rates above $4 \times 10^{-6}\,M_\odot\,\mathrm{yr}^{-1}$, models retain convective envelopes up to the end of accretion, potentially dissipating accreted magnetic flux. Because this transition typically occurs above $\sim 1.3\,M_\odot$, our results help explain the preferential survival of fossil fields in intermediate-mass stars, provided the radiative structure persists post-accretion. We also predict an increased incidence of strongly magnetized radiative stars at metallicities below $Z=0.01$.
item.dc:creator: Luis Villarroel Casanova, Dominik R. G. Schleicher, Daniele Galli, Jaime A. Rosales

item.title: A Wolf-Rayet nebula in its disruption phase: high-resolution radio observations of PCG 11
item.description: arXiv:2611.03954v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: (abridged abstract) Wolf-Rayet stars have high mass-loss rates and fast stellar winds. Their interaction with circumstellar material from previous evolutionary phases can produce complex nebular morphologies. Hydrodynamic instabilities can fragment wind-swept material, producing condensations, filaments, and gaps that alter the confinement of stellar wind and ionizing radiation. The role of fragmentation in the late evolution and dispersal of WR nebulae remains poorly constrained. PCG 11, with its fragmented morphology and regular scalloped rim, offers an opportunity to investigate these processes. We aim to characterize the structure of PCG 11 and investigate its ring-like morphology and scalloped rim. We constrain its three-dimensional geometry and determine whether the optical fragmentation pattern is also traced by ionized gas. We obtained high-resolution radio continuum images with MeerKAT at 2.6 and 3.1 GHz and ATCA at 5.5 and 9.0 GHz. The radio emission reveals a hollow, equatorially enhanced structure viewed close to its symmetry axis. The images resolve the rim into condensations, low-brightness gaps, and finger-like protrusions. We quantify the fragmentation scale and relate it to the nebular geometry. We also detect an unresolved source coincident with WR 75ab, whose rising radio spectrum is consistent with thermal wind emission. The nebula processes only a small fraction of the stellar ionizing radiation, indicating substantial photon leakage. PCG 11 captures a poorly observed stage in massive-star bubble evolution: the swept-up shell has developed a coherent instability pattern and become fragmented and porous, while remaining dynamically coupled to the stellar wind. It provides a clear view of how fragmentation and erosion reshape the circumstellar environment during a transitional evolutionary phase.

item.title: Carbon-Reaction Constraints on Stellar Evolution: White-Dwarf Heating, Carbon-Burning Products, and Black-Hole Masses
item.description: arXiv:2611.04197v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The effects of ${}^{12}\mathrm{C}+{}^{12}\mathrm{C}$ fusion and ${}^{12}\mathrm{C}(\alpha,\gamma){}^{16}\mathrm{O}$ capture on stellar heating, composition, and black-hole masses are examined. Rates from a published Bayesian analysis of carbon fusion are used in calculations with MESA. In an accreting carbon--oxygen white dwarf, the Bayesian rates move the point at which nuclear heating equals combined neutrino and surface photon losses to slightly larger stellar masses and higher central temperatures and densities. At an accretion rate of $10^{-7}\,M_\odot\,\mathrm{yr}^{-1}$, the Bayesian median gives a central temperature approximately $2.57\%$ higher and a central density $18.9\%$ higher than the calculation using the standard CF88 rate. A separate calculation follows carbon burning in an initially $20\,M_\odot$, $Z=0.0142$ star. Relative to the CF88 rate with MESA's standard division between proton and alpha channels, the Bayesian-median rate with the proton-to-alpha ratio of Yang et al. increases the neon-20 mass remaining at central carbon depletion by $10.8\%$ and decreases the sodium-23 mass by $28.7\%$. For helium capture on carbon, the nuclear constraint $S_{\rm tot}(300\,\mathrm{keV})=118\pm17\,\mathrm{keV\,b}$ is applied to the published $Z=10^{-5}$ stellar models of Farag et al. Linear interpolation gives a maximum black-hole mass below the pair-instability gap of approximately $61.5$--$77.4\,M_\odot$ within the assumptions of those models. New MESA calculations at $Z=0.00142$ give smaller bound masses before collapse. Differences in the stellar assumptions prevent attributing the difference between the two curves to metallicity alone.
item.dc:creator: Akram Mukhamedzhanov

item.title: Up in smoke: carbon-destruction in the terrestrial planet-forming region of a young Class I disk
item.description: arXiv:2611.04557v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Earth's surface and deep mantle are strongly depleted in carbon compared to the Sun. Sublimation of solid carbonaceous material in the inner midplanes of young disks could cause this depletion. We study such thermal processing in HOPS-68, a Class I protostar with a rich hydrocarbon spectrum. A companion paper has shown that it is recondensing refractory dust from a hot inner disk region, and that oxygen-bearing species are tracing a warm (300-500 K) molecular layer entrained in a disk-wind. In this work, we analyze the carbon species in the JWST spectrum of this source using local thermal equilibrium slab models. We detect warm (~400 K) HCN and C2H2 at the base of a disk wind, as well as colder (~40 K) C4H2, CH3, and CS in the outer disk or outflow cavity wall. Additionally, 13CCH2, CH4, and C6H2 are detected, while ALMA observations reveal C2H tracing the outflow cavity walls. We suggest that in a "refractory carbon destruction zone" in the inner disk, carbon-bearing species are released from the grains, possibly contributing to the observed carbon depletion of Earth. The disk wind then redistributes carbon carried by HCN and C2H2 from the inner disk to the colder outer disk, where UV-induced gas-phase reactions with C2H in the outflow cavity walls could produce the aliphatic carbon chains seen. This result implies that the Warm Carbon Chain Chemistry (WCCC, e.g. N. Sakai & S. Yamamoto 2013) might trace outflows rather than infall. The formation of aliphatic chains in the disk wind could promote the abundant aliphatic organics found in meteorites and asteroids.
item.dc:creator: F. J. Ballieux, M. K. McClure, E. A. Bergin, M. L. R. Van 't Hoff, {\L}. Tychoniec, L. Francis, E. F. Van Dishoeck

item.title: A Detailed Polarimetric Imaging Study of Type II Solar Radio Burst with the MWA: Detection of Linear Polarization
item.description: arXiv:2611.04567v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Type II radio bursts, produced by magnetohydrodynamic shocks propagating through the solar corona and interplanetary medium, serve as powerful diagnostics of shock properties and ambient coronal magnetic fields. While circular polarization in type II bursts has been extensively studied, most investigations rely on dynamic spectra (DS), providing only spatially integrated measurements. DS obscures spatial variations of the polarization sign and magnitude, potentially causing cancellation effects and misrepresenting true polarization levels. We present a full-polarimetric imaging study of a metric type II burst observed with the Murchison Widefield Array at 78--133 MHz. Remarkably, we report the first detection of linear polarization in a metric type II burst, reaching a polarization fraction of $\sim12\%$ with significant spectro-temporal variability across observing bands. The spectro-temporal, spatial, and morphological properties found in this study establish linear polarization as a new diagnostic of large-scale coronal and interplanetary magnetic field structure through full-Stokes imaging of metric solar radio bursts -- challenging conventional paradigms predicting negligible linear polarization from coherent plasma emission processes.
item.dc:creator: Puja Majee, Devojyoti Kansabanik, Divya Oberoi

item.title: MAGIC's interferometric diameters of $\theta$ Ophiuchi and $\beta$ CMa and comparison with asteroseismic modelling
item.description: arXiv:2611.04650v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: $\beta$ Cephei type stars are massive ($8-25$M$_{\odot}$) and known to have several pulsation modes with periods typically of a few hours. Despite a better understanding of their physics since 1992, the inner structure of these stars involves key stellar physics processes that are still uncertain. Asteroseismology offers insights into these variable stars by analysing pulsation modes, helping to probe their inner layers and understand their structure and mixing processes. We measure the angular diameter of two $\beta$ Cephei stars, $\theta$ Oph and $\beta$ CMa, using the MAGIC Stellar Intensity Interferometer and compare them, together with the Gaia and Hipparcos parallaxes, to the predictions of the asteroseismic model. The latter are based on Levenberg-Marquardt local minimisation of stellar evolution model parameters to fit observed pulsation modes. In the case of $\theta$ Oph, the observed angular diameters are compatible with the asteroseismic model. For $\beta$ CMa, the radius derived from the angular diameter and the Hipparcos parallax is in tension, at the $2.5\sigma$ level, with the asteroseismic prediction. We show that this tension mirrors a pre-existing conflict between independent spectroscopic determinations of the surface gravity of the star, that percent-level systematics of the stellar models are quantitatively insufficient to explain it, and that it most likely points to a bias of the Hipparcos parallax. In the frame of this paper, the statistical uncertainty on the interferometric results is similar to the systematic uncertainty on the parallaxes. With the already implemented addition in early 2024 of the first Large-Sized Telescope (CTAO-North LST-1) to the setup, the uncertainty in the angular diameter of these stars is expected to decrease by an order of magnitude, allowing to further constrain stellar evolution models and parallaxes.

item.title: Solar extreme-ultraviolet waves and other associated solar activities
item.description: arXiv:2611.04833v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Extreme ultraviolet (EUV) waves are large-scale, tsunami like disturbances on the solar surface associated with eruptive phenomena such as solar flares, filament eruptions, and coronal mass ejections (CMEs). Because their strong correlation with major solar eruptions, we present here a comprehensive statistical study of EUV waves and their connections to Moreton waves, CMEs, solar flares, type II radio bursts, and solar energetic particle (SEP) events during Solar Cycle 25 (December 2019-December 2025). This study utilizes EUV data from the Atmospheric Imaging Assembly onboard the Solar Dynamics Observatory and coronagraph data from the Large Angle and Spectrometric Coronagraph onboard Solar and Heliospheric Observatory. Our analysis reveals that 12.3% of the observed EUV waves are associated with Moreton waves, 95% with CMEs, 92.7% associated with flares, 44.3% with metric type II radio bursts, and 11.8% with SEPs. While nearly all EUV waves are linked to CMEs, their association with solar flares varies significantly, ranging from weak B-class events to major X-class flares. Furthermore, the majority of Moreton waves correlate with large- or medium-class flares, with only a small fraction associated with weaker C-class flares. Our findings may contribute to a better understanding of space weather events and, potentially, to their forecasting.
item.dc:creator: Apoorv Dashora, Ramesh Chandra, Pooja Devi

item.title: Eigenfrequency sensitivity in nonadiabatic stellar pulsations
item.description: arXiv:2611.04966v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We derive an adjoint formulation of eigenfrequency sensitivity for linear nonadiabatic stellar pulsations, including the frequency dependence of the boundary conditions. Local sensitivity kernels and their cumulative integrals describe the responses of the excitation rate and oscillation frequency to prescribed scaling of the pulsation matrix and its acoustic, thermal and coupling blocks. Applications to selected radial modes of post-AGB envelopes reveal distinct spatial and subsystem sensitivity profiles. In the cool model, the ordinary mode has weak sensitivity near both boundaries for the slow branch outer boundary conditions, whereas the strange mode exhibits pronounced sensitivity in the outer layers. Selected modes of the hotter model also show appreciable outer-layer sensitivity. The block decomposition reveals differing contributions and cancellations in the excitation-rate and oscillation-frequency responses.
item.dc:creator: Jan Zalewski

item.title: The Galah survey and symbiotic stars. II. Discovery, validation, and intensive follow-up of 44 new systems accreting at the lowest detectable levels
item.description: arXiv:2611.05200v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We report the discovery, validation, and characterization of 44 new symbiotic stars (SySts) accreting at the lowest detectable levels (Lacc =< 3 Lsun). Candidates were initially selected from the Galah survey among non-pulsating M-type red giants exhibiting Halpha excess. Between 2021 and 2025, these targets were subjected to intensive multi-wavelength campaigns, including ground-based, high-resolution Echelle spectroscopy over 544 nights, multi-epoch flickering searches down to 1 mmag, and UV/X-ray observations with the Swift satellite. Our high-resolution spectra allowed for a detailed investigation of Halpha flux and line-profile variability. Crucially, the radial velocities measured for the M-giant components yielded reliable spectroscopic orbits for 22 objects and preliminary orbits for an additional eight, corroborated by binary-induced modulations in ASAS-SN photometry. Measured accretion levels vary by factors of up to 20X, emphasizing the need for high-sensitivity, long-term monitoring. Swift X-ray data exclude neutron star companions in all targets, consistent with predominance of white-dwarf degenerates in known SySts. Combined with the 33 objects from Paper I, this sample of 77 new SySts significantly exceeds the number of previously known, accreting-only Galactic symbiotic stars, constituting the bulk of the low-accretion (LowAcc) variety discovered to date and representing >10 percent of all known SySts in the Galaxy. As SySts likely spend most of their lifetimes in LowAcc faint states, characterizing this population is essential for estimating the total Galactic SySt population and evaluating the role of SySts as Type Ia supernova progenitors or sources of UV excess in elliptical galaxies.

item.title: Metamorphic novae. I. Gaia22alz -- Violent relaxation starting from static evolution
item.description: arXiv:2611.05297v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Gaia22alz (nova Vel 2022) shows characteristic properties in its light curves and spectral evolution similar to slow novae HR Del, V723 Cas, and V5558 Sgr. Their outburst begins in a way of hydrostatic expansion with no mass loss, followed by large amplitude ($\Delta V \sim 2$ mag) multiple peaks around the mean magnitude of $M_V \sim -5.5$, and eventually it decays similarly to normal classical novae. We present a light curve model of Gaia22alz based on our metamorphic nova theory: a nova starts from a static expansion and then metamorphoses to an optically thick wind evolution through a large amplitude multiple peak phase as a violent relaxation process. Our theoretical light curve for the rising phase consistently explains the slow rise and early spectral evolution of Gaia22alz. Gaia22als is a close binary as well as other three novae, which is consistent with our metamorphic nova theory that the companion motion in the nova envelope triggers the metamorphic transition. Our results do not support E. Aydi et al.'s explanation that the slow optical rise of Gaia22alz is owing to the irradiation of X-ray/UV flash.
item.dc:creator: Mariko Kato, Izumi Hachisu

item.title: Galactic-Scale Distribution of 10Be and Its Implications for the Early Solar System 10Be/9Be
item.description: arXiv:2611.03808v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Meteoritic inclusions indicate that the early Solar System contained a substantial abundance of the short-lived radionuclide 10Be. Whether it was inherited from the parent molecular cloud or requires local irradiation or late injection remains debated. Here we present the first three-dimensional simulations of a Milky Way-like disc that follow the multi-phase interstellar medium, cosmic rays (CRs), and the production and transport of 10Be by galactic CRs (GCRs) and in supernova remnants (SNRs). Nearly all 10Be is produced by GCR interactions; SNRs contribute at most about ten percent of the 10Be inherited by newly formed stars. The 10Be/9Be ratio traces the CR energy density, declining smoothly with galactocentric radius, and because stars form where supernovae inject CRs, their natal gas is CR-enriched roughly fivefold relative to the mean interstellar medium, which one-zone estimates miss. Accounting for a possibly higher Galactic star formation rate 4.6 Gyr ago, inheritance of GCR-produced 10Be can then explain the early Solar System's 10Be/9Be in our models, without late injection or local irradiation. Even when GCR-induced 10Be production in dense gas is reduced tenfold, the meteoritic value is reached in the innermost disc and missed by only a factor of a few elsewhere, so the main conclusion is robust to uncertain low-energy GCR penetration. The inferred birth radius of the Sun depends strongly on the CR diffusivity, ranging between 3 and 8 kpc, suggesting that improved modelling of low-energy CR transport could sharpen constraints on the birthplace of the Solar System.
item.dc:creator: Yusuke Fujimoto, Steven J. Desch, Jiro Shimoda, Shu-ichiro Inutsuka

item.title: The vertical distribution of molecular gas in the fourth quadrant of the Milky Way
item.description: arXiv:2611.04168v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The vertical distribution of molecular gas in the Milky Way disk is poorly studied, especially in the 4th quadrant and the far side of the Galaxy. While surveys over 20 years ago suffered from coarse beam and non-Nyquist sampling, most of the recent surveys are limited to $|b|<1^\circ$ and/or focus on the Northern Galactic plane. We examine the molecular gas's vertical distribution and properties in the fourth quadrant to check the impact of Galactic structure on current star formation. We mapped two arm tangent regions ($l=[329^\circ.0,327^\circ.0]$ for the Norma-Outer arm, and $l=[310^\circ.0,308^\circ.5]$ for the Scutum-Centaurus arm) with the $^{12}$CO 3-2 line using the 7-pixel LASMA receiver of the APEX 12 m telescope, covering up to $b=[-2^\circ,+2^\circ]$ (or $|z|\sim200$ pc near the tangent points). The noise level of the $^{12}$CO 3-2 line is about 0.4 K [$T_{MB}$] in velocity channels of 0.5 km s$^{-1}$. The vertical distribution around the tangent regions of the spiral arm is fitted with two Gaussian components, the narrow one with an FWHM thickness of 25 pc and the wide one of about 100 pc. Two explanations are proposed: they are two sub-components of the thin disk (the narrowest tracing the spiral arm and the other the inter arms components), or they trace both thin and thick disks that show a smaller thickness when observed with CO 3-2 than when observed with CO 1-0. The latter indicates that the density distribution of the interstellar medium exhibits a steeper gradient at larger heights above the plane. Clumps in the two tangent regions are searched and divided into groups by relative height. Compared with the low relative height clumps ($|z|<50$ pc), the median relative height clumps ($50~\mathrm{pc}<|z|<100~\mathrm{pc}$) have lower excitation temperature and surface density, with fewer high values in the distribution. A similar tentative trend is found for the mass.
item.dc:creator: L. -H. Lin, F. Wyrowski, S. Neupane, D. Colombo, K. M. Menten

item.title: The Survival Paradox of Close-In Planets Orbiting Red Clump Giants
item.description: arXiv:2611.04544v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Close-in planets orbiting core-helium-burning red-clump (RC) giants directly challenge tidal-engulfment theory, which predicts that planets within about 1 au of Sun-like stars should be engulfed during red-giant-branch (RGB) expansion. The existence of such survivors would imply missing physical processes in the late stages of stellar and planetary evolution. Yet only one such "forbidden" planet had been identified to date. Here we report three systems-24 Boo b, HD 12648 b, and TYC 4282-605-1 b-whose host stars are confirmed red-clump giants through asteroseismology, showing that each has already undergone dramatic expansion and contraction following helium ignition. Their planets now reside at orbital separations smaller than the maximum stellar radii attained during the RGB phase, implying that they should not have survived. Among them, 24 Boo b orbits at only 0.183 au with a 30-day period, making it the closest planet known around a red-clump giant. These discoveries demonstrate that this paradox is not an isolated anomaly but signals the emergence of a new class of evolved planetary systems. Their survival defies current models of stellar-planetary coevolution and points to unexplored physics shaping planetary architectures around post-RGB stars.

item.title: SN 2019qem: decades of extreme mass loss before the explosion of a luminous, long-lived Type IIn supernova
item.description: arXiv:2611.05328v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present the luminous, long-lived Type IIn SN 2019qem and use it to reconstruct how much mass its progenitor lost and when. We combine host-subtracted optical and mid-infrared photometry and 26 optical spectra from -22 to +699 d. We model the bolometric light curve with thin-shell CSM-interaction models in REDBACK, with the shock velocity constrained by the H$\alpha$ line widths, and compare them with an analytic interaction model. SN 2019qem rose in $\approx30$d to $M_I = -20.5$mag and a bolometric peak of $7.0\times10^{43}$ erg s$^{-1}$, and radiated $6.9\times10^{50}$ erg in the optical within 575 d, closely resembling luminous, strongly interacting SNe IIn such as SN 2010jl and SN 2015da. A Heii/Niii flash feature at -22 d and unresolved narrow Balmer lines reveal dense, slow CSM. From +78 to +445 d the H$\alpha$ wings are shaped by electron scattering, and the line stays blueshifted by 400-700 km s$^{-1}$, which points to an optically thick, asymmetric interaction region rather than to newly formed dust. In the preferred model, $\approx7 M_\odot$ of ejecta run into $\approx9 M_\odot$ of gas ejected $\approx2$ yr before explosion and then into a wind of $\approx0.6 M_\odot$ yr$^{-1}$ (for $v_w = 100$ km s$^{-1}$), sweeping up $\approx32 M_\odot$ by +544 d. The mid-infrared excess brightens for two years while the optical fades, tracing dust heated by the ongoing interaction. The host is a low-mass, star-forming galaxy, $\log(M_*/M_\odot) = 9.19$, with a sub-solar metallicity at the explosion site. In its final decades the progenitor of SN 2019qem lost mass far faster than any steady stellar wind, ending with an eruption of $\approx9 M_\odot$ two years before core collapse, consistent with luminous-blue-variable-like eruptive mass loss. Taken at face value, the mass budget implies an initial progenitor mass of $\gtrsim40 M_\odot$.

item.title: Direct evidence of non-ideal MHD in the solar wind and switchbacks
item.description: arXiv:2605.14114v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The low frequency solar wind and its switchbacks are sometimes characterized as ideal-MHD plasmas containing Alfvenic turbulence and, sometimes, as non-ideal plasmas whose turbulence cannot be Alfvenic. The reason for this ambiguity is that definitive measurements of electric fields in the plasma rest frame at fluid frequencies have not been made and such measurements rule out the possibility of one or the other of the two modes. The FIELDS electric field measurement on the Parker Solar Probe is capable of such measurements which are reported in this paper. At radial distances less than 40 solar radii on orbit 10, perpendicular and parallel electric fields in the plasma rest frame at frequencies of 0.01 to 0.1 Hz and over a broad frequency range are observed. The parallel electric fields survive in the presence of calibration errors because their amplitude, but not their existence, is affected by them. Errors in the perpendicular electric field or the solar wind velocity can produce large errors in the plasma rest frame perpendicular electric field because it is the difference of two large quantities, the electric field and the negative velocity-cross-magnetic-field. Evidence is presented that this does not happen, at least much of the time. Because both perpendicular and parallel electric fields in the plasma rest frame are observed at low frequencies, the solar wind and its switchbacks reside in a non ideal magnetohydrodynamic environment. Consequently, standard ideal MHD treatments, including ideal Alfven, slow, and fast wave formulations, cannot adequately describe the turbulent solar wind dynamics. Similar considerations may apply in other astrophysical plasmas.

item.title: Small-Scale Dynamo for Full Spectrum of Hydrodynamic Turbulence in Kazantsev Model
item.description: arXiv:2604.01718v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A method is proposed for computing coefficients in the Kazantsev equation of small-scale dynamo for the full spectrum of hydromagnetic turbulence comprising the inertial range together with the range of viscous dissipation. The dynamo equation with so-defined coefficients is solved numerically for magnetic (Rm) and hydrodynamic (Re) Reynolds numbers from $10^2$ to $10^8$. The threshold value ${\rm Rm}_c$ for onset of dynamo increases initially with Re but then saturates at a constant value of ${\rm Rm}_c \simeq 300$ for ${\rm Re}\geq 10^5$. In the case of small Prandtl number Pm = Rm/Re << 1, the field growth rate is also small and depends logarithmically on Rm. In this case, the magnetic energy spectrum peaks around the scale of Ohmic dissipation, which decreases with increasing Pm. The decrease stops at the scale of viscous dissipation while the growth rate increases sharply when Pm approaches the value of one. The increase in the growth rate proceeds to ${\rm Pm} > 1$ but slows down and then saturates at a value somewhat below the inverse lifetime of most short-living eddies. An explanation of the results is proposed.
item.dc:creator: Leonid Kitchatinov

item.title: Hybrid stars with hyperons: structure based on QCD sum rule coupling constants
item.description: arXiv:2606.20111v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present a comprehensive study of hybrid stars composed of hadrons, leptons, and quarks within a relativistic mean-field framework. Using coupling constants derived from QCD sum rules (QCDSR), we first determine the bulk properties of nuclear matter and evaluate the single-particle potentials of nucleons and hyperons to constrain the hadronic sector. The equation of state (EOS) under beta equilibrium is then constructed employing the $\sigma-\omega-\rho$ model for the hadronic phase, while the quark phase is described using both the MIT bag model and the Nambu-Jona-Lasinio (NJL) model. The hadron-quark phase transition is analyzed through both Gibbs and Maxwell constructions. Based on resulting EOSs, we obtain the mass-radius relations of hybrid stars, investigate particle fractions and their radial distributions, and calculate the tidal Love number ($\mathcal{K}_{2}$) and the dimensionless tidal deformability ($\varLambda$). Our results provide quantitative predictions relevant for comparison with current multimessenger astrophysical observations.
item.dc:creator: F. Moradi Jangal, H. R. Moshfegh, K. Azizi

item.title: A living catalog of stream interaction regions in the Parker Solar Probe era
item.description: arXiv:2610.35506v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Stream interaction regions (SIRs) and corotating interaction regions (CIRs) are important phenomena in heliospheric physics. These large-scale structures vary temporally and spatially, both in latitude and with radial distance. The additions of Parker Solar Probe (PSP) and Solar Orbiter have allowed for investigations into the radial evolution of these structures over a wide range of heliocentric distances for the first time since the Helios era. To better enable investigations of SIRs and CIRs within the inner heliosphere, we have developed a living catalog of SIR and CIR observations by Parker Solar Probe with corresponding observations by STEREO-A as well as ACE and Wind at 1 au. The methodology used for the identification of events and the generation of this catalog, the initial catalog of PSP observations spanning orbits one through five along with corresponding 1 au observations, and information on accessing the living catalog for future studies is described. This list of SIR and CIR events from PSP and corresponding observations from other heliophysics missions will enable case studies utilizing unique orbital arrangements, as well as aid in future statistical studies to further understand the properties and evolution of these structures.

item.title: Delayed maximum energy solar energetic particle events: Statistical analysis from Solar Orbiter
item.description: arXiv:2610.35520v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Investigations of solar energetic particles (SEPs) have long utilized the dispersive nature of onset times, as in, the earlier arrival of higher-energy particles compared to lower-energy particles, to infer information such as the path length to the acceleration site at the time of initial particle release. However, recent observations by Solar Orbiter and Parker Solar Probe have begun to characterize SEP events with an apparent delay in arrival times of the higher energy portion of the particle distribution, above a critical energy separating the delayed particles from that of the typical velocity dispersion signature at lower energies. Features of these delayed maximum energy (DME) SEP events, sometimes referred to as "inverse velocity dispersion" events, could provide new insight into the impacts of magnetic connectivity to locations along an expanding coronal mass ejection-driven (CME-driven) shock wave, variations of acceleration along the shock surface, and transport effects in the inner heliosphere. This study focuses on the occurrence rate and characteristics of DME events observed by Solar Orbiter relative to their footpoint locations with respect to the initial flare site. These DME events show a bias in occurrence rate towards events when the observer's footpoints were westward of the associated flare location. Additionally, estimated locations at which the highest-energy particles of DME events are released into the flux tube suggest continued release of increasingly higher-energy particles from the CME-driven shock into the connected flux tube well into the inner heliosphere. This indicates that DME events could be attributed to inner heliospheric effects and are not actually coronal in origin. This finding is consistent with previous observations and interpretations of SEP events connected westward of the associated flare.

item.title: On the Proper 3D Modeling of Orbits in Wide Binary Gravity Tests
item.description: arXiv:2610.40388v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A gravitationally-bound system of wide binary stars with precise 3D relative displacement $\mathbf{r}$ and velocity $\mathbf{v}$ can allow a Keplerian orbit reconstruction for an assumed gravitational parameter $G$. A sufficiently large sample of such systems can also be used to directly infer $G$ specific to the sample. A recent study argued that treating the semi-major axis ($a$) explicitly free with an empirical prior imposed on it can dramatically change the inference of $G$ in the Chae et al. sample of 36 wide binaries. Here we introduce and test a Bayesian Markov chain Monte Carlo algorithm that allows $a$ to be explicitly free (with or without a prior on $a$), and find using the $\alpha$-Cen AB - proxima system and the Chae et al. sample that the explicit-$a$ algorithm with an observational constraint is fully equivalent to the implicit-$a$ algorithm with an internal consistency relation involving the sky-projected separation $s$. For the $\alpha$-Cen AB - proxima system, we present orbits in Milgromian (MOND) as well as Newtonian gravity models. We show that a recent claim of Newtonian gravity from the Chae et al. sample is a consequence of a fatal error in the code or arbitrarily enlarged errors. We discuss how wide binaries can be properly analyzed and modeled to probe gravity at low acceleration and test gravity models, including the necessity of deriving individual-specific parameters, the importance of follow-up observations for anomalous systems, and the relevance of Bayesian MCMC approaches.
item.dc:creator: Kyu-Hyun Chae, Hyoseok Park, Youngsub Yoon
